name: FL-19
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+14 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Schwartzel's fundraising edge of roughly 35-to-1 over Arias
Prediction markets price a Republican hold near 94%
Open seat with no public polling keeps uncertainty elevated
model.rationale: A fourteen-point Republican district, a roughly 35-to-1 fundraising gap, and markets pricing a Republican hold near 94% all point the same direction; the open seat and the absence of polling are the only reasons uncertainty stays wide.
model.watch: Fresh polling or significant outside spending on the Democratic side showing a single-digit race would be the main trigger for revision.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Byron Donalds is leaving the seat to run for governor, but the district's fundamentals remain firmly Republican. The Southwest Florida seat leans about fourteen points toward the GOP, and Republicans have held it comfortably. Jim Schwartzel enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly two million dollars to Victor Arias's under sixty thousand, while independent Seth Haskin's campaign is minimally funded.

Prediction markets give the Republican nominee about a 94 percent chance of holding the seat, and no public polls or expert ratings contradict that picture. The open-seat nature of the contest and the lack of polling are the main sources of uncertainty, but nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race. The expected outcome is a Republican hold by roughly fifteen points.
